evidence_chunks.content: Under more extreme conditions, discharge tests at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Fig. 4a) revealed that cells with SA-based electrolyte delivered discharge capacities of 758.6, 702.2 and $638.2\mathrm{mAh}$ at $0.2\mathrm{C}$ , $0.5\mathrm{C}$ , and $1\mathrm{C}$ ( $1\mathrm{C} = 900\mathrm{mA}$ ), respectively, outperforming those with the baseline electrolyte, which exhibited 706.3, 636.8 and $563.6\mathrm{mAh}$ . These results confirm that SA facilitates higher energy density and improved capacity retention at low temperatures, rendering it well-suited for emergency storage applications in cold environments. In addition, the rate capability of sodium-ion batteries at ambient temperature is critical for practical deployment. High-rate performance enables rapid charge/discharge cycles, a requirement for power-intensive applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics [27a,28]. As shown in Fig. 4d, the SA containing system exhibited superior rate capacity, indicating enhanced commercial viability. Long-term cycling at 1C was also evaluated at room temperature (Figs. 4c and S7). During extended cycling, the baseline electrolyte showed faster polarization growth, whereas the SA-based system demonstrated superior capacity retention and enhanced coulombic efficiency. These characteristics contribute to reduced energy losses and extended battery lifespan, which are advantageous for grid-scale and commercial energy storage [29].

- 配方原文 [0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec4::child0]：Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a mixture of EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt%) to prepare Baseline electrolyte (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ). TMSBS additive (1 wt%) was added to the Baseline electrolyte to form a functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode contained 95% HC, 1.5% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0% styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was used as the separator. The mass loading of the cathode and anode was 33.0 and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

source_refs.raw_quote: Under more extreme conditions, discharge tests at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Fig. 4a) revealed that cells with SA-based electrolyte delivered discharge capacities of 758.6, 702.2 and $638.2\mathrm{mAh}$ at $0.2\mathrm{C}$ , $0.5\mathrm{C}$ , and $1\mathrm{C}$ ( $1\mathrm{C} = 900\mathrm{mA}$ ), respectively, outperforming those with the baseline electrolyte, which exhibited 706.3, 636.8 and $563.6\mathrm{mAh}$ . These results confirm that SA facilitates higher energy density and improved capacity retention at low temperatures, rendering it well-suited for emergency storage applications in cold environments. In addition, the rate capability of sodium-ion batteries at ambient temperature is critical for practical deployment. High-rate performance enables rapid charge/discharge cycles, a requirement for power-intensive applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics [27a,28]. As shown in Fig. 4d, the SA containing system exhibited superior rate capacity, indicating enhanced commercial viability. Long-term cycling at 1C was also evaluated at room temperature (Figs. 4c and S7). During extended cycling, the baseline electrolyte showed faster polarization growth, whereas the SA-based system demonstrated superior capacity retention and enhanced coulombic efficiency. These characteristics contribute to reduced energy losses and extended battery lifespan, which are advantageous for grid-scale and commercial energy storage [29].

source_refs.raw_quote: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

source_refs.raw_quote: Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a mixture of EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt%) to prepare Baseline electrolyte (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ). TMSBS additive (1 wt%) was added to the Baseline electrolyte to form a functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode contained 95% HC, 1.5% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0% styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was used as the separator. The mass loading of the cathode and anode was 33.0 and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

source_refs.raw_quote: Sodium tetrakis[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]borate (NaTFPB, 99 % purity, sourced from Aladdin Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd.) were acquired as functional additives. Prior to their utilization, these additives underwent a rigorous freeze-drying process under vacuum conditions at $-80^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ for a duration of $24\mathrm{h}$ to remove $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ . The Base electrolyte was prepared by dissolving sodium hexafluorophosphate $(\mathrm{NaPF}_6, 1.0\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1})$ in a mixture of ethylene carbonate (EC) and dimethyl carbonate (DMC) (at a mass ratio of 1:1) containing $5.0\%$ fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). The Base electrolyte serves as the reference for comparing the effect of the additive on the electrochemical performance of the cells. To formulate electrolytes containing functional additives, NaTFPB was added to the Base electrolyte at various concentrations, as illustrated in Fig. S1. All electrolyte preparations were carried out within an argon-filled glovebox environment, which was rigorously maintained to ensure that both water and oxygen levels were kept below $0.01~\mathrm{ppm}$ , thereby safeguarding the integrity and purity of the electrolytes.

source_refs.raw_quote: The influence of incorporating various concentrations of NaTFPB on the NFM111 cathode was investigated through electrochemical measurements employing NFM111||Na half-cells. The rate capabilities of the half-cells with different electrolytes are depicted in Fig. 2a. Notably, the electrolyte containing 1.0 wt% NaTFPB exhibits superior rate performance, especially at high currents, due to its low interfacial resistance compared to the electrolytes with other concentrations. Even returned to 0.5 C, the discharged capacity of the electrolyte containing 1.0 wt% NaTFPB remains notably higher than that of the other electrolytes, recovering to 133.36 mAh g $^{-1}$ . Moreover, cyclic stability tests of the different electrolytes were conducted at a current density of 1.0 C (Fig. 2b). The results reveal that the 1.0 wt% NaTFPB electrolyte delivers a capacity retention of 70 % after 500 cycles at a current density of 1.0 C, significantly outperforming the Base electrolyte and other additive concentrations. Consequently, the concentration of NaTFPB additives was standardized to 1.0 wt%. Corresponding charge–discharge curves are presented in Fig. 2c-e. During the initial formation at a current density of 0.1 C, the electrolyte with 1.0 wt% NaTFPB delivered an ultra-high discharge specific capacity of 150.39 mAh g $^{-1}$ , compared to the capacity of 134.84 mAh g $^{-1}$ for the Base electrolyte (Fig. 2c).

source_refs.raw_quote: It is worth emphasizing that the pouch cell with the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibits significant advantages in cycling performance compared to those of the previous research findings (Fig. S20). Moreover, the NaTFPB additive also significantly enhances the cycling stability of pouch cells under high temperature and high voltage conditions (Fig. 7d). Under harsh conditions of 4.1 V and 45 °C, the pouch cell with Base electrolyte experienced a sharp capacity retention drop to 80 % after only 112 cycles (Fig. S21). This is attributed to the continuous decomposition of organic solvents, leading to severe gas generation within the pouch cell. In contrast, the NaTFPB additive stabilizes the interface by forming robust SEI/CEI layers enriched with NaF and boron compounds, significantly suppressing gas generation (Fig. S22). As a result, the pouch cell with NaTFPB maintained an exceptional capacity retention of 96 % after 250 cycles. The parallel sample error analysis in Fig. S23 further confirms the superior consistency and stability of the NaTFPB system, with smaller deviations in both initial capacity and capacity retention rate compared to the Base electrolyte, highlighting its reliability for practical applications. When the working temperature decreases to -20 °C, the pouch cell with NaTFBP additive displays discharge capacities of 1.07 Ah at 0.5 C under a high voltage of 4.1 V (Fig. 7e), much higher than that with the Base electrolyte (1.01 Ah).

source_refs.raw_quote: The NFM111||HC pouch cells (1.4 Ah) are assembled to validate the significant potential of the additive in practical applications. Fig. 7a visually presents the cycling performance of the NFM111||HC pouch cell within the voltage range of 2.0–3.95 V at 25 °C. The cell containing the NaTFPB additive maintains a high capacity retention of 79 % after 500 cycles at a current density of 1.0 C, whereas the cell with the Base electrolyte retains only 62 % of its capacity. The rapid capacity degradation of the Base electrolyte cell is attributed to the poor stability of CEI/SEI and continuous decomposition of the electrolyte. The digital photographs of cycled electrodes reveal that the Base system exhibits yellow and white decomposition products while the electrodes with NaTFPB appear clean (Fig. S19). The charge–discharge curves in Fig. 7b-c display the initial discharge capacity of the NaTFPB electrolyte system reaching 1.35 Ah during the first cycle, significantly outperforming the Base electrolyte system's 1.27 Ah. After 500 cycles, the discharge capacity of the Base electrolyte system drops to 0.79 Ah, while the NaTFPB system still maintains an impressive capacity of 1.07 Ah. It is worth emphasizing that the pouch cell with the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibits significant advantages in cycling performance compared to those of the previous research findings (Fig. S20).

source_refs.raw_quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

source_refs.raw_quote: Low-temperature cyclability is one of the key advantages of sodium-ion batteries. However, reduced kinetics at low temperatures hinder the efficient intercalation of sodium ions into hard carbon, leading to metallic sodium deposition on electrode surfaces, which results in capacity degradation and safety concerns. To address this issue, we investigated the effects of the PFPN additive on low-temperature performance using a 0.4 Ah-level NFM-HC pouch cell. The cells underwent a formation process at a 0.1 C rate, as shown in the formation curves in Figure S1. The charge and discharge curves of both cells were nearly identical. Subsequent EIS analysis after formation revealed that cells with the electrolyte containing 10 wt % PFPN exhibited lower resistance (Figure 1a), indicating that the PFPN additive effectively reduces interfacial resistance in the cells. The low-temperature cyclability of cells with the baseline electrolyte and 10 wt % PFPN additive was evaluated at 0 °C and 0.2 C rate (Figure 1b–d). Notably, the cell with 10 wt % PFPN additive demonstrated approximately 4% higher capacity retention compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%) after 450 cycles (Figure 1b). During cycling, the average Coulombic efficiency of the baseline electrolyte was 99.939%, whereas the electrolyte containing 10 wt % PFPN achieved 99.951%.

In summary, we have successfully synthesized a multifunctional SA electrolyte additive for pouch NFM/HC sodium-ion batteries, enabling stable electrochemical performance across a wide operating temperature range ( $-20$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). The multifunctional role of the SA-containing electrolyte can be attributed to a combination of synergistic effects, including the regulation of $Na^{+}$ solvation structure to accelerate interfacial reaction kinetics and enhance electrochemical stability at low temperatures, the scavenging residual water to preserve the structural stability of the cathode and suppress excessive gas evolution, thereby enhancing high-temperature performance, and the preferential redox decomposition of SA on the anode surface to form a high-quality interfacial film that protects the electrode and reduces interfacial resistance. Collectively, this work provides new insights into the rational design and optimization of electrolyte additives for practical all-climate pouch SIBs and other advanced energy storage systems.

4. Conclusions
In summary, we have successfully synthesized a multifunctional TMSBS additive for the advanced electrolyte of pouch NFM/HC cells, achieving exceptional performance across an extended operational temperature range ( $-30-60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). The multifunctional mechanism of TMSBS-containing electrolytes can be elucidated through three synergistic pathways: (i) optimization of the solvation structure to promote faster reaction kinetics, achieve better performance at low temperatures, and elevate the electrochemical stability window of the electrolyte; (ii) preferential oxidation-reduction decomposition on the anode surface to form a high-quality interfacial film to protect the electrode and reduce the impedance of the battery; (iii) capture of HF and moisture, ensuring the structural stability of the cathode material and suppressing the production of excess gas to improve high-temperature performance. Therefore, this study provides new ideas for the design and optimization of electrolyte additives for commercial all-climate pouch SIBs and other energy storage devices.

source_refs.raw_quote:
A B S T R A C T
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

2.1. Preparation of the batteries
Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a mixture of EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt%) to prepare Baseline electrolyte (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ). TMSBS additive (1 wt%) was added to the Baseline electrolyte to form a functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode contained 95% HC, 1.5% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0% styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was used as the separator. The mass loading of the cathode and anode was 33.0 and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

4. Conclusion
In summary, a bifunctional electrolyte additive of NaTFPB has been demonstrated to stabilize the CEI and SEI layers in Ah-scale sodium-ion pouch full cells. NaTFPB participates in preferential redox decomposition, forming ultra-thin and robust interfacial films on both the NFM111 cathode and HC anode surfaces. Thus, the NaTFPB-induced SEI/CEI layers effectively protect the electrodes and inhibit electrolyte decomposition. The Ah-scale NFM111||HC pouch cells containing NaTFPB maintain a high capacity retention rate of up to 79 % after 500 cycles at 1 C, significantly surpassing the Base system's 62 %. The NFM111||HC pouch cell with NaTFPB also exhibits excellent high-temperature cycling performance and low-temperature discharging ability under a high voltage of 4.1 V. This work provides a promising strategy for designing bifunctional electrolyte additives to stabilize interfaces in sodium-ion batteries, paving the way for high-performance and durable energy storage systems, while future studies could focus on exploring material compatibility and synergistic effects with other additives to further enhance performance.

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min.

At both high and low temperatures, the addition of ADN made the discharge capacity increase significantly, especially with the amount of 3%. This is because the additive ADN induces the formation of SEI film with low impedances. In particular, 3% ADN led to the formation of the SEI film with the lowest impedance and resulted in the lowest polarization. As a result, the batteries of G3 exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at low temperatures. In addition, the batteries of G3 also exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at high temperatures, indicating that the SEI film formed from the induction of ADN has a better stability at high temperatures. On the contrary, the discharge capacity retention rates of the batteries of G1 are the lowest at both high and low temperatures, demonstrating that the SEI film formed by the electrolyte without the additive ADN has large impedance and poor stability at high temperatures. To further understand the different rate and low-temperature performance of the batteries with different volume of electrolyte additive, the electrochemical impedance of each battery was tested (Fig. 5D). The electrochemical impedance spectra of the batteries of G1, G2, G3, and G4 showed flat semicircles in the high-frequency regions.

4. CONCLUSIONS
In summary, the incorporation of PFPN as an electrolyte additive has successfully led to significant enhancements in both the low-temperature performance of sodium-ion batteries and the flame retardancy of the electrolyte. The NFM-HC pouch cell with 10 wt % PFPN exhibited a capacity retention of 85% after 450 cycles at 0.2 C rate and 0 °C, representing an approximate 4% increase in capacity compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%), and a capacity retention of 84% after 600 cycles at 0.5 C and 30 °C. The SEI layer is thinner and possesses superior kinetic properties compared to the baseline, effectively preventing sodium plating and enhancing the cycle life. This research highlights the potential of PFPN in sodium ion battery applications requiring long-life and low-temperature operation, offering new insights into electrolyte modification using P- and F-containing additives.

The NFM cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode active materials were procured from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode slurry consisted of 94.5 wt% NFM, 1.8 wt% PVDF, 1 wt% carbon nanotubes (CNT), 2.5 wt% Super P, and 0.2 wt% maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP), and was cast onto aluminum foil. The HC anode was composed of 95 wt% HC,

1.5 wt% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2 wt% styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 wt% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd.) was employed as the separator. citations.chunk_id: 0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec2::child0
citations.quote: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

citations.quote:
In summary, we have successfully synthesized a multifunctional SA electrolyte additive for pouch NFM/HC sodium-ion batteries, enabling stable electrochemical performance across a wide operating temperature range ( $-20$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). The multifunctional role of the SA-containing electrolyte can be attributed to a combination of synergistic effects, including the regulation of $Na^{+}$ solvation structure to accelerate interfacial reaction kinetics and enhance electrochemical stability at low temperatures, the scavenging residual water to preserve the structural stability of the cathode and suppress excessive gas evolution, thereby enhancing high-temperature performance, and the preferential redox decomposition of SA on the anode surface to form a high-quality interfacial film that protects the electrode and reduces interfacial resistance. Collectively, this work provides new insights into the rational design and optimization of electrolyte additives for practical all-climate pouch SIBs and other advanced energy storage systems.

citations.quote: Under more extreme conditions, discharge tests at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ (Fig. 4a) revealed that cells with SA-based electrolyte delivered discharge capacities of 758.6, 702.2 and $638.2\mathrm{mAh}$ at $0.2\mathrm{C}$ , $0.5\mathrm{C}$ , and $1\mathrm{C}$ ( $1\mathrm{C} = 900\mathrm{mA}$ ), respectively, outperforming those with the baseline electrolyte, which exhibited 706.3, 636.8 and $563.6\mathrm{mAh}$ . These results confirm that SA facilitates higher energy density and improved capacity retention at low temperatures, rendering it well-suited for emergency storage applications in cold environments. In addition, the rate capability of sodium-ion batteries at ambient temperature is critical for practical deployment. High-rate performance enables rapid charge/discharge cycles, a requirement for power-intensive applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics [27a,28]. As shown in Fig. 4d, the SA containing system exhibited superior rate capacity, indicating enhanced commercial viability. Long-term cycling at 1C was also evaluated at room temperature (Figs. 4c and S7). During extended cycling, the baseline electrolyte showed faster polarization growth, whereas the SA-based system demonstrated superior capacity retention and enhanced coulombic efficiency. These characteristics contribute to reduced energy losses and extended battery lifespan, which are advantageous for grid-scale and commercial energy storage [29].

2.1. Preparation of the batteries
Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a mixture of EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt%) to prepare Baseline electrolyte (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ). TMSBS additive (1 wt%) was added to the Baseline electrolyte to form a functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode contained 95% HC, 1.5% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0% styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was used as the separator. The mass loading of the cathode and anode was 33.0 and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

citations.quote:
4. Conclusion
In summary, a bifunctional electrolyte additive of NaTFPB has been demonstrated to stabilize the CEI and SEI layers in Ah-scale sodium-ion pouch full cells. NaTFPB participates in preferential redox decomposition, forming ultra-thin and robust interfacial films on both the NFM111 cathode and HC anode surfaces. Thus, the NaTFPB-induced SEI/CEI layers effectively protect the electrodes and inhibit electrolyte decomposition. The Ah-scale NFM111||HC pouch cells containing NaTFPB maintain a high capacity retention rate of up to 79 % after 500 cycles at 1 C, significantly surpassing the Base system's 62 %. The NFM111||HC pouch cell with NaTFPB also exhibits excellent high-temperature cycling performance and low-temperature discharging ability under a high voltage of 4.1 V. This work provides a promising strategy for designing bifunctional electrolyte additives to stabilize interfaces in sodium-ion batteries, paving the way for high-performance and durable energy storage systems, while future studies could focus on exploring material compatibility and synergistic effects with other additives to further enhance performance.

citations.quote: It is worth emphasizing that the pouch cell with the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibits significant advantages in cycling performance compared to those of the previous research findings (Fig. S20). Moreover, the NaTFPB additive also significantly enhances the cycling stability of pouch cells under high temperature and high voltage conditions (Fig. 7d). Under harsh conditions of 4.1 V and 45 °C, the pouch cell with Base electrolyte experienced a sharp capacity retention drop to 80 % after only 112 cycles (Fig. S21). This is attributed to the continuous decomposition of organic solvents, leading to severe gas generation within the pouch cell. In contrast, the NaTFPB additive stabilizes the interface by forming robust SEI/CEI layers enriched with NaF and boron compounds, significantly suppressing gas generation (Fig. S22). As a result, the pouch cell with NaTFPB maintained an exceptional capacity retention of 96 % after 250 cycles. The parallel sample error analysis in Fig. S23 further confirms the superior consistency and stability of the NaTFPB system, with smaller deviations in both initial capacity and capacity retention rate compared to the Base electrolyte, highlighting its reliability for practical applications. When the working temperature decreases to -20 °C, the pouch cell with NaTFBP additive displays discharge capacities of 1.07 Ah at 0.5 C under a high voltage of 4.1 V (Fig. 7e), much higher than that with the Base electrolyte (1.01 Ah).

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. citations.quote: $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min.

citations.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

citations.quote: The specific discharge capacities at different temperatures are shown in Fig. 4. At both high and low temperatures, the addition of ADN made the discharge capacity increase significantly, especially with the amount of 3%. This is because the additive ADN induces the formation of SEI film with low impedances. In particular, 3% ADN led to the formation of the SEI film with the lowest impedance and resulted in the lowest polarization. As a result, the batteries of G3 exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at low temperatures. In addition, the batteries of G3 also exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at high temperatures, indicating that the SEI film formed from the induction of ADN has a better stability at high temperatures. On the contrary, the discharge capacity retention rates of the batteries of G1 are the lowest at both high and low temperatures, demonstrating that the SEI film formed by the electrolyte without the additive ADN has large impedance and poor stability at high temperatures. To further understand the different rate and low-temperature performance of the batteries with different volume of electrolyte additive, the electrochemical impedance of each battery was tested (Fig. 5D). The electrochemical impedance spectra of the batteries of G1, G2, G3, and G4 showed flat semicircles in the high-frequency regions.

Abstract: A commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with a capacity of 650 mAh is fabricated using the ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and the hard carbon as the cathode and anode materials, respectively. $1.0\mathrm{MNaPF}_6$ in the mixed carbonate solvents is served as the electrolyte. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, adiponitrile (ADN) has a stronger ability of electron donating than the carbonate solvents and thus is easier to be reduced on the surface of the cathode material to form the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, so ADN is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time.

association_citations.quote: $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min.

citations.quote: Low-temperature cyclability is one of the key advantages of sodium-ion batteries. However, reduced kinetics at low temperatures hinder the efficient intercalation of sodium ions into hard carbon, leading to metallic sodium deposition on electrode surfaces, which results in capacity degradation and safety concerns. To address this issue, we investigated the effects of the PFPN additive on low-temperature performance using a 0.4 Ah-level NFM-HC pouch cell. The cells underwent a formation process at a 0.1 C rate, as shown in the formation curves in Figure S1. The charge and discharge curves of both cells were nearly identical. Subsequent EIS analysis after formation revealed that cells with the electrolyte containing 10 wt % PFPN exhibited lower resistance (Figure 1a), indicating that the PFPN additive effectively reduces interfacial resistance in the cells. The low-temperature cyclability of cells with the baseline electrolyte and 10 wt % PFPN additive was evaluated at 0 °C and 0.2 C rate (Figure 1b–d). Notably, the cell with 10 wt % PFPN additive demonstrated approximately 4% higher capacity retention compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%) after 450 cycles (Figure 1b). During cycling, the average Coulombic efficiency of the baseline electrolyte was 99.939%, whereas the electrolyte containing 10 wt % PFPN achieved 99.951%.

citations.quote: This optimized SEI structure not only enhances interfacial kinetics but also effectively suppresses sodium plating on the hard carbon electrode, significantly improving the cell's performance. The pouch cell exhibits remarkable cycling stability, with a capacity retention of 85% after 450 cycles at 0.2 C and 0 °C and 84% after 600 cycles at 0.5 C and 30 °C. This work highlights the potential of PFPN as a high-performance electrolyte additive for long-life and low-temperature SIBs, offering new insights into electrolyte design for advanced energy storage systems. citations.quote: The cathodes were composed of active material NFM, an electrical conductor, and a binder, with a mass ratio of 95:3:2, coated onto Al foil. The cathodes exhibited an average mass loading of 15 mg cm $^{-2}$ and a tap density of 2.95 g cc $^{-1}$ . The anodes consisting of hard carbon (HC) as the active material, electrical conductor, and binder in a mass ratio of 95.3:1:3.7 were coated onto Al foil, achieving an average mass loading of 8.2 mg cm $^{-2}$ and a tap density of 0.95 g cc $^{-1}$ . Notably, the width and length of the anodes were designed to be 0.1 mm larger than those of the cathodes to ensure proper alignment and prevent short circuits. To construct the pouch cells, the cathodes and anodes were interleaved layer-by-layer, separated by a 20 $\mu$ m poly(ethylene) (PE) membrane. The assembled cell was then sealed in a laminated aluminum film bag. For the baseline electrolyte, we employed an electrolyte formulation with certain engineering application value based on prior research conducted by our group. $^{30}$ The specific formulation is as follows: 16.7954 g of NaPF $_{6}$ was dissolved in a 100 mL solvent mixture comprising propylene carbonate (PC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) in a volume ratio of 50:47:3, supplemented with 2 wt % 1,3,2-dioxathiolane-2,2-dioxide (DTD) as an additive. The optimized electrolytes were prepared by adding an appropriate amount of the PFPN additive.

However, reduced kinetics at low temperatures hinder the efficient intercalation of sodium ions into hard carbon, leading to metallic sodium deposition on electrode surfaces, which results in capacity degradation and safety concerns. To address this issue, we investigated the effects of the PFPN additive on low-temperature performance using a 0.4 Ah-level NFM-HC pouch cell. The cells underwent a formation process at a 0.1 C rate, as shown in the formation curves in Figure S1. The charge and discharge curves of both cells were nearly identical. Subsequent EIS analysis after formation revealed that cells with the electrolyte containing 10 wt % PFPN exhibited lower resistance (Figure 1a), indicating that the PFPN additive effectively reduces interfacial resistance in the cells. The low-temperature cyclability of cells with the baseline electrolyte and 10 wt % PFPN additive was evaluated at 0 °C and 0.2 C rate (Figure 1b–d). Notably, the cell with 10 wt % PFPN additive demonstrated approximately 4% higher capacity retention compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%) after 450 cycles (Figure 1b). During cycling, the average Coulombic efficiency of the baseline electrolyte was 99.939%, whereas the electrolyte containing 10 wt % PFPN achieved 99.951%.

citations.quote:
4. CONCLUSIONS
In summary, the incorporation of PFPN as an electrolyte additive has successfully led to significant enhancements in both the low-temperature performance of sodium-ion batteries and the flame retardancy of the electrolyte. The NFM-HC pouch cell with 10 wt % PFPN exhibited a capacity retention of 85% after 450 cycles at 0.2 C rate and 0 °C, representing an approximate 4% increase in capacity compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%), and a capacity retention of 84% after 600 cycles at 0.5 C and 30 °C. This improvement is attributed to the formation of a SEI layer rich in P and N elements on the electrode surface. The SEI layer is thinner and possesses superior kinetic properties compared to the baseline, effectively preventing sodium plating and enhancing the cycle life. This research highlights the potential of PFPN in sodium ion battery applications requiring long-life and low-temperature operation, offering new insights into electrolyte modification using P- and F-containing additives.

In addition, the rate capability of sodium-ion batteries at ambient temperature is critical for practical deployment. High-rate performance enables rapid charge/discharge cycles, a requirement for power-intensive applications such as electric vehicles and portable electronics [27a,28]. These characteristics contribute to reduced energy losses and extended battery lifespan, which are advantageous for grid-scale and commercial energy storage [29].

evidence_ledger.quote:
4. Conclusion
In summary, a bifunctional electrolyte additive of NaTFPB has been demonstrated to stabilize the CEI and SEI layers in Ah-scale sodium-ion pouch full cells. NaTFPB participates in preferential redox decomposition, forming ultra-thin and robust interfacial films on both the NFM111 cathode and HC anode surfaces. Thus, the NaTFPB-induced SEI/CEI layers effectively protect the electrodes and inhibit electrolyte decomposition. The Ah-scale NFM111||HC pouch cells containing NaTFPB maintain a high capacity retention rate of up to 79 % after 500 cycles at 1 C, significantly surpassing the Base system's 62 %. The NFM111||HC pouch cell with NaTFPB also exhibits excellent high-temperature cycling performance and low-temperature discharging ability under a high voltage of 4.1 V. This work provides a promising strategy for designing bifunctional electrolyte additives to stabilize interfaces in sodium-ion batteries, paving the way for high-performance and durable energy storage systems, while future studies could focus on exploring material compatibility and synergistic effects with other additives to further enhance performance.

evidence_ledger.quote: In summary, the incorporation of PFPN as an electrolyte additive has successfully led to significant enhancements in both the low-temperature performance of sodium-ion batteries and the flame retardancy of the electrolyte. The NFM-HC pouch cell with 10 wt % PFPN exhibited a capacity retention of 85% after 450 cycles at 0.2 C rate and 0 °C, representing an approximate 4% increase in capacity compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%), and a capacity retention of 84% after 600 cycles at 0.5 C and 30 °C. This improvement is attributed to the formation of a SEI layer rich in P and N elements on the electrode surface. The SEI layer is thinner and possesses superior kinetic properties compared to the baseline, effectively preventing sodium plating and enhancing the cycle life. This research highlights the potential of PFPN in sodium ion battery applications requiring long-life and low-temperature operation, offering new insights into electrolyte modification using P- and F-containing additives.

4. CONCLUSIONS
In summary, the incorporation of PFPN as an electrolyte additive has successfully led to significant enhancements in both the low-temperature performance of sodium-ion batteries and the flame retardancy of the electrolyte. The NFM-HC pouch cell with 10 wt % PFPN exhibited a capacity retention of 85% after 450 cycles at 0.2 C rate and 0 °C, representing an approximate 4% increase in capacity compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%), and a capacity retention of 84% after 600 cycles at 0.5 C and 30 °C. This improvement is attributed to the formation of a SEI layer rich in P and N elements on the electrode surface. The SEI layer is thinner and possesses superior kinetic properties compared to the baseline, effectively preventing sodium plating and enhancing the cycle life. This research highlights the potential of PFPN in sodium ion battery applications requiring long-life and low-temperature operation, offering new insights into electrolyte modification using P- and F-containing additives.

citations.quote: A multifunctional additive, 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA), was synthesized from the readily available saccharin, then 1 % SA was added into carbonate-based electrolytes to enhance the performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) employing $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM) cathodes and hard carbon (HC) anodes across a wide temperature range from $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . The commercial pouch cells delivered a capacity retention of 90.52 % after 300 cycles at room temperature and 92.28 % after 300 cycles at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ . Low-temperature rate performance at $-20\ ^{\circ}C$ and cycling at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ further demonstrated the excellent adaptability of SA-containing electrolytes under sub-zero temperature. Moreover, under high-voltage operation at 4.0 V, the SA-containing electrolyte effectively suppressed capacity fading, resulting in an 11.44 % improvement in capacity retention. Compared to conventional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte enables interfacial optimization by suppressing excessive growth of cathode and anode interphases, also it eliminates detrimental electrolyte components, tune the solvation structure and promote interfacial reaction kinetics. In situ gas analysis conducted during cycling at $45\ ^{\circ}C$ revealed that SA significantly inhibits gas-evolving side reactions, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs.

In summary, we have successfully synthesized a multifunctional SA electrolyte additive for pouch NFM/HC sodium-ion batteries, enabling stable electrochemical performance across a wide operating temperature range ( $-20$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). The multifunctional role of the SA-containing electrolyte can be attributed to a combination of synergistic effects, including the regulation of $Na^{+}$ solvation structure to accelerate interfacial reaction kinetics and enhance electrochemical stability at low temperatures, the scavenging residual water to preserve the structural stability of the cathode and suppress excessive gas evolution, thereby enhancing high-temperature performance, and the preferential redox decomposition of SA on the anode surface to form a high-quality interfacial film that protects the electrode and reduces interfacial resistance. Collectively, this work provides new insights into the rational design and optimization of electrolyte additives for practical all-climate pouch SIBs and other advanced energy storage systems.

4. Conclusions
In summary, we have successfully synthesized a multifunctional TMSBS additive for the advanced electrolyte of pouch NFM/HC cells, achieving exceptional performance across an extended operational temperature range ( $-30-60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). The multifunctional mechanism of TMSBS-containing electrolytes can be elucidated through three synergistic pathways: (i) optimization of the solvation structure to promote faster reaction kinetics, achieve better performance at low temperatures, and elevate the electrochemical stability window of the electrolyte; (ii) preferential oxidation-reduction decomposition on the anode surface to form a high-quality interfacial film to protect the electrode and reduce the impedance of the battery; (iii) capture of HF and moisture, ensuring the structural stability of the cathode material and suppressing the production of excess gas to improve high-temperature performance. Therefore, this study provides new ideas for the design and optimization of electrolyte additives for commercial all-climate pouch SIBs and other energy storage devices.

citations.quote:
A B S T R A C T
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

2.1. Preparation of the batteries
Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a mixture of EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt%) to prepare Baseline electrolyte (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ). TMSBS additive (1 wt%) was added to the Baseline electrolyte to form a functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode contained 95% HC, 1.5% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0% styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was used as the separator. The mass loading of the cathode and anode was 33.0 and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.

citations.quote:
A B S T R A C T
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

citations.quote:
4. Conclusions
In summary, we have successfully synthesized a multifunctional TMSBS additive for the advanced electrolyte of pouch NFM/HC cells, achieving exceptional performance across an extended operational temperature range ( $-30-60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). The multifunctional mechanism of TMSBS-containing electrolytes can be elucidated through three synergistic pathways: (i) optimization of the solvation structure to promote faster reaction kinetics, achieve better performance at low temperatures, and elevate the electrochemical stability window of the electrolyte; (ii) preferential oxidation-reduction decomposition on the anode surface to form a high-quality interfacial film to protect the electrode and reduce the impedance of the battery; (iii) capture of HF and moisture, ensuring the structural stability of the cathode material and suppressing the production of excess gas to improve high-temperature performance. Therefore, this study provides new ideas for the design and optimization of electrolyte additives for commercial all-climate pouch SIBs and other energy storage devices.

4. Conclusion
In summary, a bifunctional electrolyte additive of NaTFPB has been demonstrated to stabilize the CEI and SEI layers in Ah-scale sodium-ion pouch full cells. NaTFPB participates in preferential redox decomposition, forming ultra-thin and robust interfacial films on both the NFM111 cathode and HC anode surfaces. Thus, the NaTFPB-induced SEI/CEI layers effectively protect the electrodes and inhibit electrolyte decomposition. The Ah-scale NFM111||HC pouch cells containing NaTFPB maintain a high capacity retention rate of up to 79 % after 500 cycles at 1 C, significantly surpassing the Base system's 62 %. The NFM111||HC pouch cell with NaTFPB also exhibits excellent high-temperature cycling performance and low-temperature discharging ability under a high voltage of 4.1 V. This work provides a promising strategy for designing bifunctional electrolyte additives to stabilize interfaces in sodium-ion batteries, paving the way for high-performance and durable energy storage systems, while future studies could focus on exploring material compatibility and synergistic effects with other additives to further enhance performance.

Under harsh conditions of 4.1 V and 45 °C, the pouch cell with Base electrolyte experienced a sharp capacity retention drop to 80 % after only 112 cycles (Fig. S21). When the working temperature decreases to -20 °C, the pouch cell with NaTFBP additive displays discharge capacities of 1.07 Ah at 0.5 C under a high voltage of 4.1 V (Fig. 7e), much higher than that with the Base electrolyte (1.01 Ah).

The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min.

citations.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

citations.quote: The specific discharge capacities at different temperatures are shown in Fig. 4. At both high and low temperatures, the addition of ADN made the discharge capacity increase significantly, especially with the amount of 3%. This is because the additive ADN induces the formation of SEI film with low impedances. In particular, 3% ADN led to the formation of the SEI film with the lowest impedance and resulted in the lowest polarization. As a result, the batteries of G3 exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at low temperatures. In addition, the batteries of G3 also exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at high temperatures, indicating that the SEI film formed from the induction of ADN has a better stability at high temperatures. On the contrary, the discharge capacity retention rates of the batteries of G1 are the lowest at both high and low temperatures, demonstrating that the SEI film formed by the electrolyte without the additive ADN has large impedance and poor stability at high temperatures. To further understand the different rate and low-temperature performance of the batteries with different volume of electrolyte additive, the electrochemical impedance of each battery was tested (Fig. 5D). The electrochemical impedance spectra of the batteries of G1, G2, G3, and G4 showed flat semicircles in the high-frequency regions.

citations.quote: Low-temperature cyclability is one of the key advantages of sodium-ion batteries. However, reduced kinetics at low temperatures hinder the efficient intercalation of sodium ions into hard carbon, leading to metallic sodium deposition on electrode surfaces, which results in capacity degradation and safety concerns. To address this issue, we investigated the effects of the PFPN additive on low-temperature performance using a 0.4 Ah-level NFM-HC pouch cell. The cells underwent a formation process at a 0.1 C rate, as shown in the formation curves in Figure S1. The charge and discharge curves of both cells were nearly identical. Subsequent EIS analysis after formation revealed that cells with the electrolyte containing 10 wt % PFPN exhibited lower resistance (Figure 1a), indicating that the PFPN additive effectively reduces interfacial resistance in the cells. The low-temperature cyclability of cells with the baseline electrolyte and 10 wt % PFPN additive was evaluated at 0 °C and 0.2 C rate (Figure 1b–d). Notably, the cell with 10 wt % PFPN additive demonstrated approximately 4% higher capacity retention compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%) after 450 cycles (Figure 1b). During cycling, the average Coulombic efficiency of the baseline electrolyte was 99.939%, whereas the electrolyte containing 10 wt % PFPN achieved 99.951%.

citations.quote:
4. CONCLUSIONS
In summary, the incorporation of PFPN as an electrolyte additive has successfully led to significant enhancements in both the low-temperature performance of sodium-ion batteries and the flame retardancy of the electrolyte. The NFM-HC pouch cell with 10 wt % PFPN exhibited a capacity retention of 85% after 450 cycles at 0.2 C rate and 0 °C, representing an approximate 4% increase in capacity compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%), and a capacity retention of 84% after 600 cycles at 0.5 C and 30 °C. This improvement is attributed to the formation of a SEI layer rich in P and N elements on the electrode surface. The SEI layer is thinner and possesses superior kinetic properties compared to the baseline, effectively preventing sodium plating and enhancing the cycle life. This research highlights the potential of PFPN in sodium ion battery applications requiring long-life and low-temperature operation, offering new insights into electrolyte modification using P- and F-containing additives.

In summary, we have successfully synthesized a multifunctional TMSBS additive for the advanced electrolyte of pouch NFM/HC cells, achieving exceptional performance across an extended operational temperature range ( $-30-60\ ^{\circ}C$ ). A B S T R A C T
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. A B S T R A C T
A carbonate-based electrolyte containing a self-synthesized trimethylsilyl-benzenesulfonate (TMSBS) multifunctional additive is developed to enhance the all-climate performance of pouch $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from -30 to 60 °C. The pouch cells exhibit an 18.1% increase in capacity retention after 250 cycles at room temperature and an 11.3% increase after 240 cycles at 45 °C. The low-temperature discharging of different rates at -30 °C and the cycling at -10 °C demonstrate the adaptability of TMSBS-containing electrolytes at low temperatures. Compared to traditional commercial electrolytes, this electrolyte can prevent excessive dissolution of interfacial films of two electrodes, purify undesirable substances of electrolyte composition, and optimize electrode interfaces and solvation structure. In addition, based on the gas analysis in the cyclic process at 45 °C and the storage at 60 °C by employing both in-situ and non-in-situ techniques, it reveals that TMSBS can suppress the side reactions of gas evolution, thereby ensuring the safety of SIBs. This work presents a practical strategy for upgrading commercial SIBs and highlights the importance of rational electrolyte design for practical applications.

citations.quote:
4. Conclusion
In summary, a bifunctional electrolyte additive of NaTFPB has been demonstrated to stabilize the CEI and SEI layers in Ah-scale sodium-ion pouch full cells. NaTFPB participates in preferential redox decomposition, forming ultra-thin and robust interfacial films on both the NFM111 cathode and HC anode surfaces. Thus, the NaTFPB-induced SEI/CEI layers effectively protect the electrodes and inhibit electrolyte decomposition. The Ah-scale NFM111||HC pouch cells containing NaTFPB maintain a high capacity retention rate of up to 79 % after 500 cycles at 1 C, significantly surpassing the Base system's 62 %. The NFM111||HC pouch cell with NaTFPB also exhibits excellent high-temperature cycling performance and low-temperature discharging ability under a high voltage of 4.1 V. This work provides a promising strategy for designing bifunctional electrolyte additives to stabilize interfaces in sodium-ion batteries, paving the way for high-performance and durable energy storage systems, while future studies could focus on exploring material compatibility and synergistic effects with other additives to further enhance performance.

citations.quote: It is worth emphasizing that the pouch cell with the NaTFPB electrolyte system exhibits significant advantages in cycling performance compared to those of the previous research findings (Fig. S20). Moreover, the NaTFPB additive also significantly enhances the cycling stability of pouch cells under high temperature and high voltage conditions (Fig. 7d). Under harsh conditions of 4.1 V and 45 °C, the pouch cell with Base electrolyte experienced a sharp capacity retention drop to 80 % after only 112 cycles (Fig. S21). This is attributed to the continuous decomposition of organic solvents, leading to severe gas generation within the pouch cell. In contrast, the NaTFPB additive stabilizes the interface by forming robust SEI/CEI layers enriched with NaF and boron compounds, significantly suppressing gas generation (Fig. S22). As a result, the pouch cell with NaTFPB maintained an exceptional capacity retention of 96 % after 250 cycles. The parallel sample error analysis in Fig. S23 further confirms the superior consistency and stability of the NaTFPB system, with smaller deviations in both initial capacity and capacity retention rate compared to the Base electrolyte, highlighting its reliability for practical applications. When the working temperature decreases to -20 °C, the pouch cell with NaTFBP additive displays discharge capacities of 1.07 Ah at 0.5 C under a high voltage of 4.1 V (Fig. 7e), much higher than that with the Base electrolyte (1.01 Ah).

citations.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries.

citations.quote: The specific discharge capacities at different temperatures are shown in Fig. 4. At both high and low temperatures, the addition of ADN made the discharge capacity increase significantly, especially with the amount of 3%. This is because the additive ADN induces the formation of SEI film with low impedances. In particular, 3% ADN led to the formation of the SEI film with the lowest impedance and resulted in the lowest polarization. As a result, the batteries of G3 exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at low temperatures. In addition, the batteries of G3 also exhibited the highest discharge capacity retention rate at high temperatures, indicating that the SEI film formed from the induction of ADN has a better stability at high temperatures. On the contrary, the discharge capacity retention rates of the batteries of G1 are the lowest at both high and low temperatures, demonstrating that the SEI film formed by the electrolyte without the additive ADN has large impedance and poor stability at high temperatures. To further understand the different rate and low-temperature performance of the batteries with different volume of electrolyte additive, the electrochemical impedance of each battery was tested (Fig. 5D). The electrochemical impedance spectra of the batteries of G1, G2, G3, and G4 showed flat semicircles in the high-frequency regions.

citations.quote: Low-temperature cyclability is one of the key advantages of sodium-ion batteries. However, reduced kinetics at low temperatures hinder the efficient intercalation of sodium ions into hard carbon, leading to metallic sodium deposition on electrode surfaces, which results in capacity degradation and safety concerns. To address this issue, we investigated the effects of the PFPN additive on low-temperature performance using a 0.4 Ah-level NFM-HC pouch cell. The cells underwent a formation process at a 0.1 C rate, as shown in the formation curves in Figure S1. The charge and discharge curves of both cells were nearly identical. Subsequent EIS analysis after formation revealed that cells with the electrolyte containing 10 wt % PFPN exhibited lower resistance (Figure 1a), indicating that the PFPN additive effectively reduces interfacial resistance in the cells. The low-temperature cyclability of cells with the baseline electrolyte and 10 wt % PFPN additive was evaluated at 0 °C and 0.2 C rate (Figure 1b–d). Notably, the cell with 10 wt % PFPN additive demonstrated approximately 4% higher capacity retention compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%) after 450 cycles (Figure 1b). During cycling, the average Coulombic efficiency of the baseline electrolyte was 99.939%, whereas the electrolyte containing 10 wt % PFPN achieved 99.951%.

citations.quote: This optimized SEI structure not only enhances interfacial kinetics but also effectively suppresses sodium plating on the hard carbon electrode, significantly improving the cell's performance. The pouch cell exhibits remarkable cycling stability, with a capacity retention of 85% after 450 cycles at 0.2 C and 0 °C and 84% after 600 cycles at 0.5 C and 30 °C. This work highlights the potential of PFPN as a high-performance electrolyte additive for long-life and low-temperature SIBs, offering new insights into electrolyte design for advanced energy storage systems. 4. CONCLUSIONS
In summary, the incorporation of PFPN as an electrolyte additive has successfully led to significant enhancements in both the low-temperature performance of sodium-ion batteries and the flame retardancy of the electrolyte. The NFM-HC pouch cell with 10 wt % PFPN exhibited a capacity retention of 85% after 450 cycles at 0.2 C rate and 0 °C, representing an approximate 4% increase in capacity compared to the baseline electrolyte (81.33%), and a capacity retention of 84% after 600 cycles at 0.5 C and 30 °C. ## 配方筛选结果
获得文献支持的候选：cand-SA-0045、cand-TMSBS-0031。

### 候选资料：cand-SA-0045（通过筛选）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（质量）：EC=3.0, EMC=7.0；添加剂：2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA)；添加剂用量：2-sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA)=1 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0045_Lu 等 - 2025 - All-climate carbonate electrolyte with 2-sulfobenzoic anhydride additive leads the way to high-perfo::sec4::child0]：Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co., Ltd. A baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving NaPF $_6$ (1 mol/L) into a mixed solvent of EC and EMC (weight ratio 3:7). To formulate a functional electrolyte, 1 wt% 2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA) was added to the baseline system. The NFM cathode and hard carbon (HC) anode active materials were procured from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode slurry consisted of 94.5 wt% NFM, 1.8 wt% PVDF, 1 wt% carbon nanotubes (CNT), 2.5 wt% Super P, and 0.2 wt% maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP), and was cast onto aluminum foil. The HC anode was composed of 95 wt% HC,

![](images/8bfcb630e9de984c98fbfc69f2dd0cb440e9bd8293373fa0ec9806e9fb6d55de.jpg)  
Fig. 1. 2-Sulfobenzoic anhydride (SA) is introduced as electrolyte additive to enhance the electrochemical performance of pouch SIBs.

1.5 wt% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2 wt% styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5 wt% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd.) was employed as the separator. The areal mass loadings of the cathode and anode were 33.0 and 20.1 mg/cm $^{2}$ , respectively, with a negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio of 1.1 (based on theoretical capacity calculation).

### 候选资料：cand-TMSBS-0031（通过筛选）
以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。
盐：NaPF6；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（质量）：EC=3.0, EMC=7.0；添加剂：trimethylsilyl benzenesulfonate (TMSBS)；添加剂用量：trimethylsilyl benzenesulfonate (TMSBS)=1 wt%。
- 配方原文 [0031_Li 等 - 2025 - Designing an efficient all-climate carbonate-based electrolyte facilitating commercial pouch sodium-::sec4::child0]：Sodium hexafluorophosphate (NaPF $_6$ ), ethylene carbonate (EC), and methyl ethyl carbonate (EMC) were supplied by Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. NaPF $_6$ was dissolved into a mixture of EC and EMC (EC: EMC = 3:7 in wt%) to prepare Baseline electrolyte (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ). TMSBS additive (1 wt%) was added to the Baseline electrolyte to form a functional electrolyte. NFM and HC active materials were purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. and Kuraray Co., Ltd., respectively. The NFM cathode was fabricated from NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotubes (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and maleic acid dispersed in $N$ -methylpyrrolidone (NMP) at a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated onto an aluminium substrate. The HC anode contained 95% HC, 1.5% carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), 2.0% styrene butadiene rubber (SBR), and 1.5% Super P. A Celgard 2700 membrane (Xingyuan Materials Co., Ltd) was used as the separator. The mass loading of the cathode and anode was 33.0 and 20.1 mg cm $^{-2}$ , respectively. The negative-to-positive (N/P) capacity ratio was 1.1. The empty pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h, then transferred to a glove box, and injected 6.0 g of electrolyte. Other operations not mentioned were all carried out using the general methods in the battery manufacture.
